title: Unified SDK surface for streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: ship a consistent, minimal-breaking SDK surface across TypeScript, Python, and Go to support three capabilities together: streaming responses, structured output validation/parsing, and tool/function calling. This ticket covers the interface designs, example snippets across the three languages, the compatibility shim for older SDK users, and the rollout/QA plan. Deliverables: interface RFC, per-language SDK changes, migration guide, E2E tests, and a 2-week opt-in beta flag for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Interfaces defined for streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs in TS/Py/Go RFC
SDKs implement the new interfaces and pass cross-language contract tests
Backward compatibility shim translates legacy chat/stream shapes to new structured-output envelope
Migration guide published in Console docs with example code for streaming+tools in TS/Py/Go
End-to-end test suite validates: streaming chunk ordering, tool-call roundtrip, JSON Schema validation of structured outputs
Beta rollout gated by feature flag; no customer-facing breaking changes during flag period
technical_notes: We propose a thin envelope for all model outputs: {kind: 'message'|'tool_call'|'tool_result', payload: ... , metadata: {...}}. Streaming uses an ordered chunk stream where each chunk references an envelope id. Tool/function calling must include: name, args (validated against JSON Schema), and a callback token for the runner. Compatibility shim maps legacy 'delta' messages and 'function_call' fields to the new envelope shape. Performance: keep envelope small to avoid token overhead; prefer compact keys when encoding over the wire. Kernel/runtime backpressure signals must be preserved in streaming transport layer. See language-specific examples below.
python_example:
# Python example: generator-based streaming + function call + pydantic validation
from typing import TypedDict, Generator
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

class Envelope(BaseModel):
    kind: str  # 'message' | 'tool_call' | 'tool_result'
    id: str
    payload: dict

class OrderModel(BaseModel):
    total: float
    items: list

def stream_completion(prompt: str) -> Generator[Envelope, None, None]:
    # SDK yields Envelope instances as they arrive
    yield Envelope(kind='message', id='env_1', payload={'text': 'Preparing order...'})
    yield Envelope(kind='tool_call', id='env_2', payload={'name': 'check_stock', 'args': {'sku': 'SKU123', 'qty': 5}})

# Consumer handles tool calls synchronously/asynchronously depending on integration
for env in stream_completion('Order 5 of SKU123'):
    if env.kind == 'tool_call':
        # run tool; then push tool_result back to runtime
        pass
    if env.kind == 'message':
        print(env.payload.get('text'))

# Structured output validation
try:
    validated = OrderModel(**{'total': 42.0, 'items': []})
except ValidationError as e:
    # surface structured output validation errors to the Console audit logs
    print(e)
compatibility_shim: Strategy: provide a runtime-level shim (server + client helpers) that accepts legacy shapes and emits the new envelope; SDKs will include a small 'legacyCompat' helper by default with opt-out via config. Mapping rules: legacy delta/text -> Envelope(kind='message', payload={text}), legacy function_call -> Envelope(kind='tool_call', payload={name,args}), legacy function_call_result -> Envelope(kind='tool_result', payload={name,result}). The shim also implements a compact binary encoding toggle for low-bandwidth customers. Deprecation schedule: shim enabled by default during 60-day beta; warn in logs after 30 days; disabled by default after 60 days; final removal 120 days after GA. Ensure telemetry includes % of customers using shim so PM can evaluate cutover readiness.
migration_guide_notes:
- For TypeScript: replace previous streaming 'onDelta' hooks with 'for await...of' over streamCompletion() and handle Envelope kinds. Example migration helper provided in the SDK.
- For Python: generator-based streaming should be backward-compatible; call Envelope.dict() to inspect.
- For Go: StreamCompletion returns channel of *Envelope; a helper ParseLegacyDelta() is included.
- Feature flag: 'sdk_unified_streaming' available in Console; opt-in required for initial customers.
- Docs: publish migration recipes and a checklist for testing: token accounting, UI streaming/scrolling behavior, tool execution latency and retry semantics.
rollout_plan: 1) RFC + stakeholder signoff (PM, Design, Security) - complete. 2) Implement core envelope and compatibility shim in runtime (ENG-4792). 3) Ship TS SDK beta behind feature flag; outreach to 20 early-adopter teams. 4) Iterate on UX and fix any ordering/dup issues; ship Py/Go betas. 5) Remove opt-out after telemetry indicates <5% legacy usage. 6) GA release: bump SDK minor versions, add migration note in Console and changelog.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for envelope mapper + JSON Schema validator (TS/Py/Go).
- Contract tests: run cross-language test harness that asserts chunk ordering, idempotent tool-call replay, and schema validation results.
- E2E on Dedicated & Private: validate that private deployments using older agents can opt into shim and see same behavior.
- Performance benchmarks: measure median token latency increase (goal <3% overhead) and max additional tokens in envelope (goal <6 tokens).
- QA checklist links: https://qa.redwood.ai/testsuites/sdk-unified-streaming
